haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine's invoices go to the shadow store, and it never charges or touches the ledger.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store, without charging or writing the ledger.
haiku-low.q3: Seven consecutive days with under 0.1% mismatch and at least 5,000 invoices compared per day; a person makes the move.
haiku-low.q4: A new-engine charge failure rate above 2% in any 10-minute window, in both or new_only modes.
haiku-low.q5: Rollbacks end in old_only, flag set last. Afterward, gates reset to zero, the rollout returns to shadow, and the 7-day count restarts.
haiku-low.q6: It stops at day 35 after entering new_only, because skipped usage events expire from the 35-day log then.
haiku-low.q7: Workers read billing_mode from the config service; if unreachable they keep the last mode and start no new charges. In-flight invoices: NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q8: Evidence is in the rollout record, durable storage beside the ledger, holding gate counters and approvals. A person makes each forward move; the controller only proposes.
haiku-low.q9: Component not stated; it measures new-engine charge failure rate above 2% in any 10-minute window. When met, rollback starts; later triggers are ignored while it runs.
haiku-low.q10: Due charges wait; the fence stops new-engine charges and failed ones queue for the old engine. Charging happens after the last step sets old_only.
haiku-low.q11: Each engine checks the ledger for the charge key first and skips if an entry exists; the key is also the provider's idempotency key.
haiku-low.q12: Fence stays up, flag unchanged (still both or new_only), due charges wait in queue. Rollback resumes from its last recorded step.

sonnet.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine computes invoices and writes them to the shadow store (never charges, never writes the ledger).
sonnet.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing every invoice into the shadow store, without charging or writing the ledger.
sonnet.q3: A 7-day gate: seven consecutive clean days, each with mismatch rate under 0.1% and at least 5,000 invoices compared (days that can't be checked don't count). A person makes the move; the controller only proposes it.
sonnet.q4: Charge failure rate above 2 percent in any 10-minute window, in both or new_only modes (new_only only before day 35). Not in shadow (new-engine errors there never trigger rollback).
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. Before the new engine can take over again, all gates reset to zero: it returns to shadow and the 7-day count restarts, then a person must approve each forward move through the gates.
sonnet.q6: At day 35 in new_only with no rollback (the clock starts on entering new_only). The rollback path closes and the old engine may be retired (decommissioned). Reason given: skipped usage events expire from the log after 35 days, so replay must finish well before then.
sonnet.q7: NOT STATED for how workers find out beyond that they read billing_mode from the config service (only the controller writes it). If the config service is unreachable, workers keep the last mode and start no new charges. What happens to an invoice being processed at the moment of a change is NOT STATED.
sonnet.q8: The rollout record (proposed durable storage next to the ledger) holds gate day counters, approvals and Finance sign-off. The controller only proposes moves, a person must approve, and the gates (7-day, 14-day plus Finance sign-off) must be met first. Exactly what technically blocks an early promotion is NOT STATED beyond that.
sonnet.q9: NOT STATED which component detects it (the controller is implied but not stated). It measures the new engine's charge failure rate over 10-minute windows; above 2 percent in both or new_only, automatic rollback starts, and further triggers are ignored while a rollback runs.
sonnet.q10: The fence stops the new engine from starting new charges. Failed due charges are queued for the old engine and are never dropped. The old engine charges them only after rollback completes; billing_mode is set to old_only as the last step. The exact timing of the queue's charging is otherwise NOT STATED.
sonnet.q11: The ledger entry's charge key, which is also the payment provider's idempotency key. Engines check the ledger before charging and skip if an entry exists. Reconciliation also marks already-charged periods as closed (from new_only), and where reconciliation finds a difference the ledger wins and nothing is charged again.
sonnet.q12: The fence stays up, billing_mode flag stays unchanged (still both or new_only), and due charges wait in the queue. The rollback resumes from its last recorded step; the flag is never set to old_only before reconciliation completes.
